item.description: En 1995, una potente erupción del volcán Soufrière Hills sepultó gran parte de Montserrat, un territorio británico de ultramar situado en el Caribe. Tres décadas después, la isla conserva las huellas de aquella catástrofe, pero también sorprende por sus paisajes, su biodiversidad y su memoria viva. Quienes la visitan deben respetar estrictas zonas de exclusión y seguir las indicaciones de seguridad. item.title: Irrigation’s climate benefit could equal 363 years of its own emissions
item.description: U.S. irrigation produces some greenhouse gas emissions, but new research suggests it prevents vastly more by allowing farmers to grow more food on less land. Without irrigation, replacing lost crop yields could require converting natural ecosystems into farmland, releasing an estimated 6.86 gigatons of greenhouse gases. That is equivalent to about 363 years of current annual U.S. irrigation emissions. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: How a pathogen turns flowers into leaves
item.description: Scientists have found how a protein produced by bacteria disrupts the mechanism that controls flower development in plants, turning reproductive organs into leaf-like structures. These findings shed light on a plant disease that is expected to spread as climate change expands the range of its insect vectors in northern latitudes. They used a synchrotron technique at ESRF, the European Synchrotron in Grenoble, France. The results are an Editor's Pick in the Journal of Biological Chemistry. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: World’s top 20 private equity firms produce more greenhouse gases a year than most countries, report finds

item.description: A nearly 2,000-acre former farm along Wisconsin’s Sugar River is now permanently protected after years of drainage efforts and a tax dispute. item.title: Panama canal traffic to be cut again as drought from El Niño worsens
item.description: Planned daily reductions will further choke one of the world’s most important shipping lanes The Panama canal plans to again cut maritime traffic due to worsening drought caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon, further choking up one of the world’s most important shipping lanes. The canal handles 5% of global maritime trade and about 40% of US container traffic; it is favoured by shippers because it usually reduces cost and transit times, especially for companies trading between China, Asia and the US.
